title: Cross-encoder / Learned Reranking
interviewAnswer: A reranker applies a more expensive query-document model to a small candidate set from first-stage retrieval. It improves precision because it jointly represents the query and candidate rather than comparing independent embeddings.
keyPoints: Use only on a bounded candidate set.
why: Cross-encoder / Learned Reranking appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Use only on a bounded candidate set.
deepDive: A reranker applies a more expensive query-document model to a small candidate set from first-stage retrieval. It improves precision because it jointly represents the query and candidate rather than comparing independent embeddings. Latency/cost grows with candidates. Train/evaluate on realistic negatives. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Retrieve 100 documents with BM25/vector search, then cross-encode and return the best 10.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Cross-encoder / Learned Reranking make?
How would you validate or debug Cross-encoder / Learned Reranking in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
